description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of lung tissue showing fungal structures.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image of lung tissue, stained with hematoxylin and eosin, reveals a round fungal structure with internal compartments suggestive of a sporangium or spherule. Surrounding the fungal structure are inflammatory cells and disrupted lung architecture, indicative of infection. The stain highlights cellular and fungal morphology effectively.

Case_06021/figure8.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of the brain.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of brain tissue showing fungal organisms with thick walls and clear halos.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows brain tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The image highlights multiple round fungal organisms with thick walls and prominent clear halos, consistent with encapsulated yeast forms. The surrounding brain parenchyma exhibits inflammatory changes, including cellular infiltrates and tissue damage. The findings are suggestive of a fungal infection, such as cryptococcosis.
visible_findings: round fungal organisms with thick walls
tissue damage in the surrounding parenchyma

description.short_caption: MRI of the brain showing abnormal enhancement in the basal cisterns.
description.detailed_description: This axial T1-weighted MRI image with contrast shows abnormal enhancement in the basal cisterns, suggestive of inflammation or infection. The orbits and surrounding structures appear symmetric. The enhancement pattern may indicate meningitis or another infectious/inflammatory process. No obvious mass effect or midline shift is visible.
visible_findings: abnormal enhancement in the basal cisterns

description.short_caption: H&E stain of brain tissue showing fungal organisms with thick-walled capsules.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows brain tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). Numerous round to oval fungal organisms with thick-walled capsules are visible, some with a clear halo surrounding them, consistent with encapsulated yeast forms. The background shows neuropil with scattered inflammatory cells and evidence of tissue damage. The findings are suggestive of a fungal infection, such as cryptococcosis.
